answer: Imagine an agent economy that admits newcomers through one narrow inlet instead of a thousand open doors. Every applicant needs a sponsor who already holds reputation; that sponsor escrows a bond which is burned outright if the applicant turns out to be a puppet account. Faking ten thousand identities now costs ten thousand bonds, so the attack stops being cheap. Trust itself behaves like crystal growth: slow, layered, and impossible to rush overnight. Honest sponsors end up in a small grove of peers who vouch only for agents they have actually settled trades with.
